subject: Music Production
title: The Roland TR-808: The Beat That Changed Everything
description: A quick, practical guide to The Roland TR-808: The Beat That Changed Everything.

hook.text: The Roland TR-808, released in 1980, was considered a commercial failure because its drums sounded fake.

buildup.text: Its booming bass drum and snappy snare were electronic, sounding nothing like real acoustic drums.

discovery.text: Hip-hop, electro, and dance producers embraced these artificial sounds and made them iconic.

twist.text: Only twelve thousand 808s were ever made, yet its sounds appear on more hit songs than any other drum machine.

climax.text: The 808's bass kick became the heartbeat of modern hip-hop, trap, and pop music worldwide.

punchline.text: A failed drum machine became the most famous beat ever.

quiz.question: Why was the TR-808 initially considered a failure?
options: Its drums sounded fake and unlike real acoustic drums
It could only play one pattern
